findings.text: Guest state lifecycle provides creation and release. Creation returns a zeroed dynamically allocated record flagged for guest use, prepared with reset and user defaults, sized from guest defaults plus aligned register displacement, carrying default feature enablement and a portable size anchored to the hypervisor save area and widened when the host user default is larger. Release clears the holder and frees only records that are dynamically allocated, guest flagged and inactive, ignoring empty holders.

Guest control and transition services cover enabling of additional dynamic features, revision of the disable vector, synchronization on virtual exit, and bidirectional exchange of task and guest records. Enabling succeeds immediately when nothing new is requested. Revision adjusts saved enablement when the guest image is not resident to keep later restores safe. Exit synchronization refreshes memory state from the hardware disable register when dynamic sizing applies. Exchange preserves prior task linkage and activation and reports uniform success.

Portable representation conversion moves state between kernel records and external buffers in both directions. Outbound formatting uses extended layout when the processor advertises the required capability and legacy layout otherwise, marking legacy output so an extended host can restore it. Inbound conversion checks control coverage and control register legality before invoking shared import logic, preserving the current protection key setting when the incoming presence map omits that component.

Kernel mode floating point support offers entry into a protected section, synchronization of the current record, activation marking, and restoration of a known initial image after faults. Entry acquires protection when interrupts allow, records that kernel use is active, preserves user context when in process context and resident, discards stale tracking, and installs default control values for requested classes. Synchronization and activation maintain residency indicators and processor affinity for the current task.

Feature location service returns the address of a requested component inside a save area when the processor supports extended saving, the kernel has enabled that component, and the saved presence map includes it. Absence of any of those conditions yields a null result. The service warns when asked for a component the kernel has not enabled, reflecting a caller contract violation.

Kernel initiated saving writes the full enabled set described by the record feature mask into the kernel register area, split for transport into low and high halves. The operation expects patching of instruction alternatives to have completed and validates the record against the requested mask beforehand. Faults during this kernel destination save are treated as unexpected and trigger a diagnostic warning rather than a recoverable path.

The low level save primitive selects among multiple hardware save variants through runtime patching keyed to processor capabilities, defaulting to the base form. It clears a caller supplied error holder on entry and routes any fault at the save point through an exception table that records a fault code instead of propagating. The target memory and mask halves are the only inputs, with memory clobbered.

Permission management freezes guest allowances on first guest record creation and preserves them across duplication. Freezing applies only on the wide address model and sets a lock indicator alongside existing allowances under signal protection. Duplication copies both task and guest allowance records from the group owner to the child under the same protection when dynamic sizing is active. Retrieval uses single access semantics paired with the update path.

Sizing derives kernel and portable extents from configuration defaults and the register displacement with alignment. Guest creation combines the guest default extent with the aligned displacement. Reallocation combines a caller supplied kernel extent similarly and records both kernel and user extents. Initial image copying uses the full kernel default without extended support and a compact legacy plus header extent with extended support.

Dynamic feature activation accepts only bits within the dynamic user set and requires that group allowances cover all newly requested bits, otherwise denying with a permission error. A configuration without dynamic support unconditionally denies. Success captures current kernel and user extents under protection before releasing the lock and attempting reallocation, tolerating concurrent additions because captured extents remain valid for the current request.

Reallocation produces a fresh zeroed record that unions prior enablement and user enablement with newly requested bits while clearing those bits from the disable vector. It carries over allocation and confidentiality markers and activity state for guests, refreshes the compaction map from the merged enablement, and atomically publishes the new record, updating the active pointer when the replaced record was active. The predecessor is freed only when dynamically allocated.

Raw location computation requires kernel enablement of the requested component and, under compacted hardware, membership in the saved compaction map, warning and failing otherwise. The resulting address is the save area base plus a displacement derived from the compaction map and component identity. Kernel enablement itself is determined by membership in the configured maximum feature set.

Inbound portable headers are accepted only when presence bits stay within the record user allowance, the compaction map is clear indicating uncompacted format, and reserved padding is all zero with a fixed build checked length. Control register values are checked for reserved bits when related legacy or vector components are present, and missing legacy presence with vector presence still updates the stored control fields. Disabled components overlapping the disable vector are rejected.

Shadow stack propagation leaves state untouched when no new pointer is supplied or when the relevant configuration is absent. Otherwise it locates the user control area inside the child record copied from its parent and stores the supplied pointer there. Absence of that area despite a non zero pointer is treated as an unexpected condition and reported as failure.

Group signal serialization with interrupt exclusion guards allowance words and size fields during freezing, permission checks, extent capture and inheritance. Updates use single store semantics while reads use single load semantics. The critical sections are kept short, with reallocation and other potentially blocking work performed after release.

Register state serialization guards saving, restoring, swapping, disable vector updates, reallocation publication and synchronization. Holders ensure residency is settled before pointer exchange that could change layout. Some paths assert interrupt state or preemption state rather than acquiring, with exit synchronization requiring interrupts already disabled and enable paths requiring preemption allowed. Kernel entry acquires only when interrupts are enabled.

Task and guest floating point linkage centers on a record pointer with a saved task pointer for nesting, an activity indicator, allocation and guest and confidentiality markers, kernel and user extents, enablement and user enablement maps and a disable vector. Separate allowance structures hold permission bits and extents for task and guest contexts. The holder also tracks the processor of last activation and a need load indicator governs residency.

The save area combines legacy register images, a header and an extended region. The header carries a presence map, a compaction map and fixed reserved padding. Legacy coverage includes integer register bytes up to the control word, the control word with flags, remaining stack space and vector space, plus padding and software reserved bytes in extended exports. Extended components live at per component displacements with per component lengths, with gaps zeroed on export.

Hypervisor transition moves through preservation, pointer exchange and reestablishment. Preservation saves hardware content when the outgoing image is not confidential and is resident. Exchange records the task image on entry and restores it on exit while toggling the guest activity marker. Reestablishment restores registers with full coverage for ordinary images including disable handling, or refreshes only the disable state for confidential images whose content comes from protected memory, then marks active.

Dynamic enablement progresses from fault filtering through allowance verification to record replacement. Filtering discards events outside the dynamic user set as success with optional diagnostics. Verification checks group allowances under protection and snapshots extents. Replacement allocates, merges enablement, clears disable bits, initializes compaction, publishes under register protection and refreshes hardware disable state when the replaced image was active.

Outbound formatting selects a presence subset according to mode, choosing legacy only, legacy plus vector, or the intersection of saved, allowed and requested sets for full extended mode. It emits legacy pieces from live or initial sources based on presence, then for full mode emits padding, software bytes and header followed by extended components in canonical order with gap zeroing and special sourcing for the protection key component, finally zeroing any trailing space.

Inbound conversion proceeds from header retrieval through validation to per component import and header merge. Retrieval supports kernel or user origins with fault reporting. Validation covers allowance, format, reserved padding and control legality. Import copies each requested component from its portable displacement to its kernel location and extracts or clears the protection key output. Merging preserves supervisor presence while replacing user presence with the incoming map.

Asynchronous entry points restore determinism after faults and virtual transitions. Exception fixup reinstalls the initial image with full coverage. Virtual exit refresh synchronizes the in memory disable vector and cached hardware copy from the disable register when dynamic sizing is active. Kernel section entry and activation marking establish a clean control environment and record residency for subsequent use.

Failure handling distinguishes expected allocation and validation failures from unexpected internal inconsistencies. Allocation failures report memory or fault errors without side effects. Validation failures report invalid input for unknown, compacted, reserved, control or disable conflicts. Unexpected cases such as saving before patching, faults to kernel destinations, freeing of inappropriate records, missing compaction membership or missing control areas raise diagnostics and take defensive defaults.

The full state mask XFEATURE_MASK_FPSTATE defines save and restore coverage while the dynamic subset XFEATURE_MASK_USER_DYNAMIC scopes fault driven growth. Legacy group masks cover integer and vector basics with companions for vector extension and protection keys, alongside a supervisor collection and a maximum count XFEATURE_MAX. Component identities include protection key and user shadow stack variants. Copy selectors distinguish several export shapes. Hardware hooks include the disable register MSR_IA32_XFD, default control value, kernel use selectors, residency flag and fault type for save faults.

Guest residency hazards include attempting restores with disabled components present and mishandling protected memory images. The update path clears disabled presence when the image is not resident to avoid host faults on later restore. The swap path avoids register restore for confidential images and refreshes only disable state, relying on protected memory mechanisms for content. Incorrect handling would risk host exceptions or stale control state.
